hook: SCP-1296 is a delivery service with exactly one product, and its staff have no patience for questions. It is a comedy file built on phone calls and test orders, so the fun is in watching researchers try to outsmart a business that refuses to be investigated. Expect some swearing.
whyItMatters:
The entry shows how much character a joke anomaly can get from customer-service rudeness alone. The sales rep and the driver both shut down every attempt at interrogation, which turns the usual Foundation interview into a sketch about a bad hotline.

The test log then does what good comedy files do: it keeps the premise fixed and lets the orders get stranger until the last one goes somewhere darker.
thingsToNotice:
The test orders are the heart of it. An alpaca order arrives as a llama wearing a freshly skinned alpaca hide, a request for a lama brings a Buddhist monk with no memory of how he got there, and a robot llama costs thousands and behaves exactly like the real animal.

The last order asks for SCP-1545 itself. It vanishes from its locker and comes back fifteen seconds later, thrown off the car roof at speed by a second driver, with two unidentified corpses inside that had been dead at least a day; the driver yells a profane parting line as the car speeds off.

related.note: The final test order is SCP-1545, and the delivery goes badly wrong.
